newsitem.title: INDIA: India says approved $7 bln FDI in July-Dec 1996.
newsitem.headline: India says approved $7 bln FDI in July-Dec 1996.

text.p: India approved foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals worth $7.0 billion in the six months from July to December, 1996, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Wednesday.

India's United Front coalition government, which was formed in June last year, decentralised foreign investment approvals by increasing the powers of the Industry Ministry's Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) last year.

"From July to December 1996, we have cleared through the revamped Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB), 899 proposals involving a total investment of $7.0 billion," Maran was quoted by a government statement as saying in Hyderabad.
The minister, who was addressing a conference on investment in the southern Indian city, did not give the figure for the same period of 1995.
The FIPB is empowered to approve foreign investment proposals of up to 6.0 billion rupees ($167 million).
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, aims to attract $10 billion of foreign investment annually. India attracted $2.0 billion in FDI in 1995/96 (April-March).
Maran said the government had simplified procedures and speeded up approvals of foreign investment to woo investors.
"Simplicity, speed, transparency and fairness are the four pilars on which our FDI policy has been raised," Maran said.
